newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- POUND AND EQUITIES FALL AFTER ELECTION ANNOUNCEMENT

The announcement of the date of the general election by prime minister John Major coincided with a fall in the price of sterling, in shares, and in government bonds. However, analysts say much of the decline in equities and gilts is down to international rather than domestic factors, although profit-taking on sterling was attributed to pre-election jitters following the pound's seven-month rally.
-- LABOUR REFUSES TO
DROP UNION RECOGNITION PLAN

Labour party leader Tony Blair has told employers that he will not go back on a party commitment to give trade unions legal powers of recognition in the workplace. Full details of the policy will not be revealed until after the general election, but employers and business leaders have expressed fears it will mean a return to the destructive industrial relations of the 1970s.
-- BBC TO SET UP TWO JOINT VENTURES WITH FLEXTECH

The BBC has announced plans for two joint ventures with the cable and satellite channel provider Flextech. Under the deal, described as "an historic development for the BBC" by the corporation's deputy director Bob Phillis, the main joint venture will operate eight new TV channels. The second operation is designed to acquire and run UK Gold, the channel which currently broadcasts library programmes from the BBC and Thames Television. The deal will allow the BBC to exploit is huge library resources.
-- PUSH FOR PFI HOSPITAL DEAL RUNS OUT OF TIME

Government plans to rush through emergency legislation needed to facilitate hospital deals under the controversial Private Finance Initiative (PFI) have been scuppered by the announcement of the general election date. Health secretary Stephen Dorrell has admitted there is not enough parliamentary time left to proceed with the changes -- an embarrassing admission for the minister who in 1995 predicted that about a dozen contracts would be agreed last year and that the first projects would be up and running before the election.
-- LANG SPEEDS UP GAS COMPETITION
Trade secretary Ian Lang has moved to speed up the phased opening of Britain's domestic gas market to full competition.

Lang laid an order in parliament which will give industry regulator Ofgas the option to extend competition to 2.5 million customers in Scotland and north-east England in October. So far about two million customers in south and southwest England have seen trials of competition, but the new measure would mean that a total of 4.5 million of the 19 million gas-connected households would be able to choose their suppliers.
-- CAR SALES HEADING FOR RECORD SAYS ACADEMIC

Professor Garel Rhys, a leading academic on the automotive industry, has said that new car demand in the UK next year could match the record 2.3 million sales of 1989. Professor Rhys, of the Cardiff Business School, cited continuing economic growth and the reluctance of any post-election government to risk actions which might undermine consumer or business confidence.
Rhys also projected a further 200,000 sales this year -- a 10 per cent increase on 1996 -- as "a real possibility".
-- RETAILERS IN BATTLE OVER ALBUM PRICES

Price-cutting promotions by two leading UK supermarket chains have prompted a price war in the music market. Last week Tesco, Britain's number one supermarket chain, launched an advertising campaign claiming it was selling five albums at two stg less than W.H. Smith and Woolworths. Now Safeway is offering any two Top 10 albums for 20 stg. John Preston, chairman of record company BMG Entertainment, warned that the situation would become "more serious" if the supermarket price war were to spread to the rest of the music trade.
-- ROVER GROUP UNVEILS CHEAPER 4WD VEHICLE

Rover Group has released the first pictures of its new contender in the market for small four-wheel-drive vehicles. The vehicle, which will carry the company's Land Rover marque and will be called the Freelander, will be formally unveiled at the Frankfurt motor show in September. It is intended to compete in a market segment just below the company's existing Defender, Range Rover and Discovery models, and will aim to take market share from Toyota's Rav 4 and the Frontera from Vauxhall.
-- PEARSON TO INVEST 100 MILLION STG IN FT

Media, information and entertainment group Pearson has announced a 30 per cent fall in operating profit, to 181 million stg, after taking a 100 million stg charge for accounting "irregularities" at Penguin USA. Shares in the group fell 15 per cent on news of the results, which were in line with expectations but disappointed investors who had hoped for more news on the future structure of Pearson. Announcing the results, new chief executive Marjorie Scardino said the group is to invest 100 million stg in the Financial Times newspaper as part of a push to develop Pearson's main brands as well as to improve performance throughout the group.
-- HELPHIRE GETS 16 MILLION STG PRICE TAG

Bath-based Helphire, which specialises in providing car hire and repair on credit, has been valued at 16.3 million stg for a placing of six million shares. The floatation, which prices the company's shares at 100p, is intended to raise about 5.5 million stg to help fuel national expansion and wipe out some 2.4 million stg of debt. The company, which currently has five depots, is to open a further three this year and plans to increase the number to between 30 and 80 over the next five years.
